To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ALICE measurements of two-particle azimuthal correlations in Pb-Pb and pp collisions show a strong suppression of the away-side jet-like correlation in central Pb-Pb events, which is compatible with expectations for jet quenching.

1) the correlation functions show a long-range ridge and a jet peak in all collision systems, 2) the ridge is stronger for central than for peripheral collisions, 3) the ridge is more pronounced for pions than for kaons, 4) the jet peak is stronger for peripheral than for central collisions, 5) the mean transverse momentum fluctuation is smaller for peripheral than for mid-central or central collisions, 6) the net charge fluctuations are larger for mid-central

the ALICE detector is able to perform the measurements described in this abstract, that the measured correlations, fluctuations and their dependence on collision energy and multiplicity are in agreement with expectations from a hydrodynamical evolution of the system and that these results are important input for the understanding of heavy-ion collisions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the properties of the hot and dense strongly interacting matter created in heavy-ion collisions at the LHC.
a variety of topics related to correlations and fluctuations.
the investigation of the space-time evolution of the hot and dense matter produced in heavy-ion collisions at the LHC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the data show that the system created in Pb-Pb collision at the LHC energy has properties that are not compatible with a system of non-interacting particles, but that are compatible with a strongly interacting system.
the ALICE results on event-by-event fluctuations are consistent with the expectations from a hydrodynamic model.
the ALICE results on two-particle correlations are in line with a picture in which the collective expansion of the system plays a key role in the production of particles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ALICE results show a strong suppression of correlations in the away side in the most central events.

we have shown that we can measure these quantities in heavy ion collisions at the LHC, that we can measure them in a wide variety of systems, that they can be described with hydrodynamic models and that they are sensitive to the initial conditions.
we can confirm the existence of a collective behaviour in heavy-ion collisions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we observe a strong suppression of the elliptic and triangular anisotropic flow coefficients in high-multiplicity p-Pb collisions, which is consistent with the suppression observed in high-multiplicities Pb-Pb collisions.
the system created in heavy-ion collisions exhibits strong collectivity, and is close to a thermodynamic system.

the correlations are dominated by the correlations between the soft particles produced in the initial state and the hard partons produced in the initial hard scattering, while the fluctuations are dominated by the fluctuations of the initial state.
